buses.name: 6U CubeSat bus
buses.tooltip: A small satellite made of six 10 cm cubes, about the size of a cereal box. Six slots for parts inside.
buses.sourceNote: 1U is a 10 cm cube of about 1 to 1.33 kg, so 6U is at most about 8 kg. Build time: as little as 9 months, typically 18 to 24 months including parts.

buses.name: Small satellite bus
buses.tooltip: A fridge-sized satellite. Room for big instruments like radar, but it needs a bigger rocket.
buses.sourceNote: CubeSat 101: a small satellite is under 300 kg. Cost and build time are rounded estimates.

buses.name: Large satellite bus
buses.tooltip: A bus-sized satellite for big missions such as watching weather from far away.
buses.sourceNote: Rounded from typical large Earth-observation and weather satellites.

parts.name: Body solar cells
parts.tooltip: Solar cells glued to the outside of the craft. Light and cheap, but small.
parts.sourceNote: Rounded for cells covering a 6U CubeSat's sides, averaged over how the craft faces the Sun.

parts.name: Deployable solar wings
parts.tooltip: Panels that fold out after launch, like wings. They nearly double your power.
parts.sourceNote: CubeSat 101 (ChargerSat-1): deployable solar panels nearly double the power input.

parts.name: Large solar array
parts.tooltip: A big folding solar panel for larger satellites.

parts.name: Small battery
parts.tooltip: Stores solar power for when the craft is in Earth's shadow (eclipse). Light, but holds little.
parts.sourceNote: CubeSat 101: CubeSats use common lithium-ion batteries with protection circuits. Capacity is a rounded estimate.

parts.name: Large battery
parts.tooltip: A bigger lithium-ion battery pack. Heavier, but it carries the craft through long eclipses.
parts.sourceNote: CubeSat 101: lithium-ion batteries. Capacity is a rounded estimate.

parts.name: Battery pack
parts.tooltip: A large battery pack for bigger satellites.

parts.name: Flight computer
parts.tooltip: The craft's brain. Runs the parts and stores data until it can be sent to Earth.
parts.sourceNote: Rounded for a CubeSat onboard computer with flash storage.

parts.name: Magnetorquer
parts.tooltip: Electromagnets that push against Earth's magnetic field to turn the craft. Simple, but slow and rough pointing.
parts.sourceNote: Rounded for a CubeSat magnetorquer board.

parts.name: Reaction wheel
parts.tooltip: A spinning wheel that turns the craft precisely, so cameras can point exactly where you want.
parts.sourceNote: Rounded for a CubeSat reaction wheel unit.

parts.name: Cold-gas thruster
parts.tooltip: Puffs of gas that change the orbit a little, for example to bring the craft down at the end of the mission.
parts.sourceNote: Rounded for a CubeSat cold-gas system; 0.4 kg of the mass is propellant. Delta-v uses the rocket equation.

parts.name: UHF radio
parts.tooltip: A simple radio on the 437 MHz amateur band. Cheap and easy to hear, but very slow: fine for health data, too slow for images.
parts.sourceNote: CubeSat 101: many CubeSats use amateur radio bands such as 437 MHz (70 cm). 9.6 kbps is a common CubeSat UHF speed.

parts.name: S-band radio
parts.tooltip: A faster radio, about 100 times quicker than UHF. Enough for a few images per pass.
parts.sourceNote: Rounded for a CubeSat S-band transmitter.

parts.name: X-band radio
parts.tooltip: A high-speed radio that can send lots of images, but it uses more power, costs more and takes longer to get.
parts.sourceNote: Rounded for a CubeSat X-band transmitter.

parts.name: Camera
parts.tooltip: Takes colour photos, like a phone camera pointed at Earth. Sees smoke, but not the heat of a fire.
parts.sourceNote: Rounded for a CubeSat visible-light camera.

parts.name: Multispectral imager
parts.tooltip: Sees several colours of light, including some we can't. Shows dry plants, smoke and burned land.
parts.sourceNote: Rounded for a CubeSat multispectral imager.

parts.name: Thermal imager
parts.tooltip: Sees heat (infrared). Fires glow brightly to it, even through thin smoke. Slow to build.
parts.sourceNote: Rounded for a CubeSat thermal infrared imager; long lead time.

parts.name: Imaging radar
parts.tooltip: Sends out radio waves and listens for echoes, so it sees through clouds and at night. Heavy and power-hungry.
parts.sourceNote: Rounded for a small-satellite synthetic aperture radar.

parts.name: Spectrometer
parts.tooltip: Splits light into a rainbow to find out what things are made of, such as gases in the air.

parts.name: Magnetometer
parts.tooltip: Measures magnetic fields, like a very sensitive compass.
